Cable Theft Wars

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Security officers tasked with safeguarding Johannesburg’s copper cables are under attack by cable thieves who are becoming organised and armed. What would it take to put an end to this crime?

Unique Selling Point:
These guards who work for various security companies are contracted to City Power and Eskom. The two entities have recorded incidents that reveal a war on security guards who often work with little to no resources. What are these criminals looking for? Well, it’s not just cable that they want. According to police minister Beki Cele, “they are on a hunt for guns to use for future robberies”.

Summary:
On the 31st of March this year, two security guards were shot execution-style after escorting one of the power utility’s trucks to City Power’s salvage yard in Booysens, Johannesburg. The truck was loaded with copper cables that were burnt in an inner-city underground tunnel fire. I am in possession of the dash cam video of these two officers sitting in their car. Then, gunmen appeared on both sides of the car, shooting them. The killers then pulled their bodies from the vehicle and took their firearms. There have been no arrests. Please note we have the family of one of the deceased willing to speak to us. Sbongile is the sister to Themba (dead guard) who will share with us the state in which she found her brothers body. We also have video of his funeral that was held in KZN. She says because her brother worked for a security company and not City Power, the family was not compensated. His three kids are struggling l, she says. Her brother was a breadwinner.

The following day (1st April), there was an exchange of gunfire with criminals in the informal settlement, Kya Sands. A City Power security officer died after being shot in the head.

A month before both incidents, a guard was shot dead and six of his colleagues narrowly escaped death, after they were ambushed by 30 heavily-armed suspects as they attempted to steal copper cable in Soweto. Simphiwe Ndamashe is one of the officers who survived the attack. He will speak to us about what happened on that day but also share problems about his working conditions - he says they sometimes made to work without bulletproof vets or guns. He decided to quit his job because of the trauma and his realisation that these thieves are willing to kill.


Further information:
Why is this a problem?

City power and Eskom made a decision to outsource security functions due to the increase in the above-mentioned cases. So security companies like Ensamble Security (which Themba worked for) are roped in to lend a hand. Criminals know this and they are taking advantage. They know the security guards are not well equipped to do their work. And often times, they don’t have the guns to protect themselves. Point is, City Power and Eskom have distanced themselves from the killings, even though these security guards were killed protecting their assets.

But the cases are too many to ignore. From April last year to March this year City Power experienced more than 80 security related incidents. City Power has lost more than R187-million as a result of copper cable theft and damage to electricity infrastructure in the past five years.

Why should we care?

The continuous targeting of electricity network infrastructure will detrimentally affect critical economic sectors dependent on electricity, including the financial or banking sector, water services, sewerage and sanitation and its reticulation systems, health services such as hospitals and clinics, communication systems such as Telkom, Vodacom, MTN, Cell C, transportation systems such as railway network and traffic lights, criminal justice systems, which include courts, police stations and correctional centres, industrial sector and businesses, schools and individual households.

Press Release:


Cable Theft Syndicates
Earlier this year, a team of security personnel working in Soweto, were ambushed by a gang of heavily-armed suspects. One guard was shot dead. A month later, two security guards were gunned down while escorting one of City power’s utility trucks to a salvage yard in Johannesburg. The target: lucrative copper cables. Highly organised and well-armed, experts say there’s a new crop of copper cable thieves and they’ll stop at nothing to steal this lucrative commodity, including killing poorly resourced security guards tasked to protect City Power and Eskom’s essential infrastructure.
Producer: Busisiwe Gumede-Chizanje | Presenter: Masa Kekana


Script:


NATSOUND – guard checking his guns before heading out to start his night patrol
INTRO – It’s ten pm in Ga-Rankuwa, west of Pretoria. A security guard we’ll call Tshepo to protect his identity is on call and about to go on patrol.
NATSOUND – guard getting in the car, sound of car door closing and he starts the engine as we get into next VO
VO - It's a quiet night but the silence is deceptive - something he knows all too well.
In these parts, danger lurks in the shadows.
'TSHEPO' - SECURITY GUARD – Clip0028 < cover this whole upsound with visuals of him on patrol, looking around while driving
01:11 - Eish right now, the way that these cable thieves are operating, and all over, they are armed. 01:26 - And it's a lot of them.
VO – Here, under cover of darkness, violent gangs are on the prowl for copper. Used extensively in electric cables, and in high demand on the black market, they’ll stop at nothing to get their hands on it. But Tshepo is experienced enough to know their appetite for copper doesn’t stop at the cables: they stay hidden in the shadows, waiting for emergency technicians to arrive before robbing them of replacement cables, equipment, cellphones and even their vehicles.
NATSOUND – sound of car stopping and Tshepo gettng out to look around with his torch.
VO – A wave of opportunistic robberies and assaults on its staff forced Eskom into contracting the security company Tshepo works for to help protect its technicians and infrastructure.
But the added security doesn't appear to be a deterrent. If anything, it’s given the thieves a new target: the guns carried by the security escorts. < you can now break the sequence and see the interview from next VO
'TSHEPO' - SECURITY GUARD - Clip0028

01:54 - To tell you the truth it’s a risk. We pray to God and let him take the wheel.
VO – Eskom recorded eighty-five attacks on security contractors from April 2021 to March this year – each one chillingly brazen; sometimes, deadly.
BREATHER – more of Tshepo looking around
LINK – P108077 - Cable theft is not a new crime but it is getting worse. And there is something different about this crop of criminals - they are organized, heavily armed, and will stop at nothing to get what they want.
VO – Eskom employees, as well as those from Johannesburg’s energy distributor, City Power, are under attack.

And while millions are spent on additional security, it's impossible to provide an armed escort for every technician on callout duty. So, priority is given to staff on the night shift and those working in secluded areas during the day.

In late May, this technician we'll call Lerato responded to a morning callout in what is considered a low-risk area. She was working alone, and without a security escort.
'LERATO' - ESKOM TECHNICIAN - Eskom/Day 1/Card 1/Private/XDroot/Clip0006

06:30 - It was a normal day, very clear, and everything was going smooth for me.
VO – It wouldn't stay that way for long.
'LERATO' - ESKOM TECHNICIAN - Eskom/Day 1/Card 1/Private/XDroot/Clip0006

07:17 - ... there came two men. 07:23 - ... the other came behind me, the other was in front. 07:40 - ... they told me to go inside the bakkie. They said they want the bakkie. 07:55 - I said: “No, leave me and take the bakkie.” 07:55 - ... The other one said to me ... “do you want us to shoot you?!”
VO – The men forced her back into the bakkie.
'LERATO' - ESKOM TECHNICIAN - Eskom/Day 1/Card 1/Private/XDroot/Clip0006

08:05 - And mind you, the bakkie is a two passenger vehicle so they forced myself in between both of them having guns. 08:26 - As they were going out of the substation driving, in my mind I was asking myself if I’m going to sleep in mortuary, am I going to be raped? Are they going to throw me in a river?
VO – When the car eventually stopped, she realised what her captors were after. They demanded the pin number for her bank card.
'LERATO' - ESKOM TECHNICIAN - Eskom/Day 1/Card 1/Private/XDroot/Clip0006

09: 57 - One of them was left with me in that place where they took me. ... there is an ATM close by. And they said let me go to the ATM and if I find out the pin is wrong I’ll give you a call. 10:13 you just blow her brain and throw them inside the field.
VO – While one man kept watch another emptied her bank account. Lerato, still in the bakkie, silently prayed for her life to be spared.
'LERATO' - ESKOM TECHNICIAN - Eskom/Day 1/Card 1/Private/XDroot/Clip0006

10:54 - That day I thought it’s my last day on earth.
VO – But she was dumped on the side of the road, her assailants making off with the vehicle, equipment, cellphones, and – tragically - her savings.
BREATHER – creatively transition us back to Tshepo's night shots, him getting back to the
VO – It wasn’t always this way, says Tshepo. Criminals used to abandon their loot and scatter at the first sight of armed security guards. Now, they’re the first to strike.
'TSHEPO' - SECURITY GUARD - Clip0028

17:12 - If he takes his gun out first, it’s over for me.
VO – A stark reality he faced just a few months ago when he and his partner faced off with an angry mob.
'TSHEPO' - SECURITY GUARD – Clip0028

04:58 - ... the protesters where threatening the technicians, saying they won’t leave without their lights being reconnected.
VO – With his partner focused on the technicians and Tshepo scanning the growing crowd, neither noticed three armed men sneaking up on them from behind.
'TSHEPO' - SECURITY GUARD - Clip0028

06:45 - then one between them started shooting. 06:50 - He shot me on the hip. 07:08 - ... after he shot me I fell on the ground, ... another came and pointed a revolver at me and said he wants my gun.
VO – He believes the criminals are part of a syndicate operating in the area
'TSHEPO' - SECURITY GUARD - Clip0028

13:06 - I think the guns they were using are the same guns they took from our security guards in February.
VO – Lerato agrees that gangs are targeting specific hotspots.
'LERATO' - ESKOM TECHNICIAN - Eskom/Day 1/Card 1/Private/XDroot/Clip0006

16:14 - The very same day of my incident I think it’s the very same guys who hijacked me, two of my lady colleagues also were working and they took their phones at gunpoint.
BREATHER
VO – Ted Blom, an energy and utilities strategist, has studied cable theft trends for more than three decades. He says these days, the criminals are better organised than those tasked with stopping them.
TED BLOM – ENERGY EXPERT – P1018125

14:30 - ... you get segregation of duties like you get in a company. 14:43 -... the other guy is in charge of logistics and trucks that are ready to run and the other is a watchman or whatever or the gunmen sometimes.
VO – In February in Soweto, seven security guards confronted around thirty armed cable thieves. In the shootout that followed, one guard was killed. In Johannesburg’s Kya Sands just two months later, another security guard died in a hail of bullets.

Then, in yet another incident earlier this year, two guards were shot in Johannesburg's Newtown area while escorting a vehicle transporting copper cables. The horrific attack was captured on a dashcam.
UPSOUND/BREATHER – showing only beginning of video before the shooting starts, blur the men, then read next VO over the blurred video and shooting audio
VO – The rest of the footage is too violent to show you. It goes on to capture the moment the officers – trapped and defenceless inside their vehicle - are ravaged by bullets.
PAUSE...
After a volley of gunshots, the weapons fall silent, and the two security guards lie dead. Their attackers steal their service weapons and flee.
BREATHER
LINK - under newtown bridge - It was under this bridge in Newtown where security guards were gunned down execution style while doing their patrols. But these men were more than just security guards. They were breadwinners who were loved by their families who have now been left devastated.
GENTLE TRANSITION FROM BRIDGE TO ISAAC
ISAAC MANGENA – CITY POWER

01:14 ... the criminals themselves are too brazen and even deadly because they are heavily armed, well equipped.
VO – City Power is now at the criminal’s mercy, at a loss over how to respond to their new MO.
That’s despite spending more than R100 million on security each year and doubling the number of security guards. We caught up with their spokesperson, Isaac Mangena, near a substation known as a hotspot for cable theft and related crime.
ISAAC MANGENA – CITY POWER

04:14 - We have got a lot of substations I think almost 300 substations across the city of Johannesburg and we have about 17 000 kilometers of underground and overhead cables. 04:40 - so it would be difficult for us to basically ensure that we police every kilometer of that kind of infrastructure.
VO - Since July last year, City Power has filed more than 1 400 reports of vandalism and cable theft. Among that number were incidents targeting the technicians and their security escorts.
BREATHER – use natsound from Eskom cutaways
VO – Power utility, Eskom, isn’t being spared either.
Mashangu Shibangu, senior manager for maintenance and operations, says cable theft and related crimes are growing across the country.

MASA - 08:45 - Would you say that because it’s increasing and happening on a daily rate, you actually don’t have a hold on the situation?
SHIBANGU - 12:21- ... Our focus is supposed to make sure that we keep the lights on. 09:10 - Security is not necessarily our mandate.
MASA - 09:07 - These criminals are forcing you to pivot into security.
SHIBANGU - 09:10 - ... We do have departments that deal with security. We are just doing that as an add-on to make sure that our employees are protected.
LINK – P1018066 - It seems Eskom and city power are fighting a losing battle being outnumbered by criminals who are heavily armed and willing to kill but where are the police in all of this?
VO – The SA Chamber of Commerce and Industry estimates cable theft costs the country between R5 billion and R7 billion a year.
In June, the South African Police Service identified 18 infrastructure theft hotspots around the country. Special tasks teams are being set up in these areas and top on their agenda is cable theft and related crimes.
ISAAC MANGENA – CITY POWER

05:09 - ... We have seen a little move in terms of the number of arrests we are making due to this cable theft. We have in the past month, in July alone had about 30 suspects that were arested due to this cable theft.
VO - The SAPS declined an on-camera interview for this story but promised to respond to our questions in writing. We’re still awaiting their reply.
PAUSE...
What is certain is that they have a challenge on their hands. In 2019, we reported on a complex copper theft network: cables stolen from power lines was being sold to recycling depots before being shipped out of the country. It’s a multi-million rand enterprise. < use visuals from https://m.youtube.com/watch?v=WbAYfC0IOB0, strap them CARTE BLANCHE – MARCH 2019
Combatting this ever more treacherous crime means squeezing the channels that supply the demand.

VO – But what, if anything, can companies like Eskom and City Power do beyond contracting specialist security firms?
TED BLOM – ENERGY EXPERT – P1018125

MASHANGU SHIBANGU – ESKOM - Clip 0025

01:31 - ... We do come with technologies to try to mitigate the theft of underground cables. We do try and install detecting devices underground. 08:01 we have to make sure that we have armed response security that responds.

Please note we have the family of one of the deceased willing to speak to us. Sbongile is the sister to Themba (dead guard) who will share with us the state in which she found her brothers body. We also have video of his funeral that was held in KZN. She says because her brother worked for a security company and not City Power, the family was not compensated. His three kids are struggling l, she says. Her brother was a breadwinner. The following day (1st April), there was an exchange of gunfire with criminals in the informal settlement, Kya Sands. A City Power security officer died after being shot in the head. A month before both incidents, a guard was shot dead and six of his colleagues narrowly escaped death, after they were ambushed by 30 heavily-armed suspects as they attempted to steal copper cable in Soweto. Simphiwe Ndamashe is one of the officers who survived the attack. He will speak to us about what happened on that day but also share problems about his working conditions - he says they sometimes made to work without bulletproof vets or guns. He decided to quit his job because of the trauma and his realisation that these thieves are willing to kill. Further information: Why is this a problem? City power and Eskom made a decision to outsource security functions due to the increase in the above-mentioned cases. So security companies like Ensamble Security (which Themba worked for) are roped in to lend a hand. Criminals know this and they are taking advantage. They know the security guards are not well equipped to do their work. And often times, they don’t have the guns to protect themselves. Point is, City Power and Eskom have distanced themselves from the killings, even though these security guards were killed protecting their assets. But the cases are too many to ignore. From April last year to March this year City Power experienced more than 80 security related incidents. City Power has lost more than R187-million as a result of copper cable theft and damage to electricity infrastructure in the past five years. Why should we care? The continuous targeting of electricity network infrastructure will detrimentally affect critical economic sectors dependent on electricity, including the financial or banking sector, water services, sewerage and sanitation and its reticulation systems, health services such as hospitals and clinics, communication systems such as Telkom, Vodacom, MTN, Cell C, transportation systems such as railway network and traffic lights, criminal justice systems, which include courts, police stations and correctional centres, industrial sector and businesses, schools and individual households. Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 12 September 2022 Press Release: Cable Theft Syndicates Earlier this year, a team of security personnel working in Soweto, were ambushed by a gang of heavily-armed suspects. One guard was shot dead. A month later, two security guards were gunned down while escorting one of City power’s utility trucks to a salvage yard in Johannesburg. The target: lucrative copper cables. Highly organised and well-armed, experts say there’s a new crop of copper cable thieves and they’ll stop at nothing to steal this lucrative commodity, including killing poorly resourced security guards tasked to protect City Power and Eskom’s essential infrastructure.
